title: Hungary and Ireland
summary: Hungary is relaxed with little sign of communism; in Northern Ireland he finds a fine Irish band.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah, and of course, I played in Hungary. Now, Hungary is--- there's no way - there's no sign of Communists there only that some of the buildings have red stars on them, but you don't see any of the people - soldiers and such in the streets and you're free to buy there; you can buy anything you want in the store. Now, in Poland and Czechoslovakia you're limited - they only allow you to take certain things out and if you would happen to buy an antique - forget it - you're not allowed to take it out. But, Hungary was---
That must have slowed you down--

Yeah - well, it was very easy--- I played Ireland several times and the last time, I played Northern Ireland and I got-- with a Irish band; I didn't believe what I was hearing; they were just fine. You know, these are big surprises - it's wonderful when you travel around like this.
